title: Word from the Woods
sceneText:
A tenant sends word over before lunch that there is something going on in the north woods.

He cannot say what, exactly. “Trees down,” he says. “Not blown down by the wind.”

variants.unmet:
You go through Hartmann’s records. The boundary between the north woods and Millridge is genuinely disputed. A survey was made the year before last and the conclusion was “the stream to be the boundary”. But that stream changed its course after last year’s spring flood.

The record stops there. How the boundary is to be reckoned after the course changed is not written down anywhere in the file.
variants.met:
You go through Hartmann’s records and find the conclusion of that survey: the stream to be the boundary.

The same stream Thierry spoke about at the market. He said that whether it goes by the old bed or the new one after the change is not in the file, because whoever wrote the file did not expect a river to move.

Where the river has moved, the trees are down now.
